newsitem.title: CHINA: China trade surplus seen at $26 billion for 1997.
newsitem.headline: China trade surplus seen at $26 billion for 1997.

text.p: China's trade surplus was forecast to soar to $26 billion for all of 1997 compared with $12.2 billion in 1996, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
Exports were expected to continue to grow sharply while imports would show a gradual recovery, it said quoting a forecast by the State Economic and Trade Commission.
Exports for the whole year were forecast to reach $180 billion, up by about 19 percent year-on-year while imports were seen growing by about 10 percent to $154 billion, it said.
Exports for the third quarter were forecast at $48 billion, up by 21 percent while imports were seen reaching $36 billion, up by nine percent from a year ago, it said.
China recorded a trade surplus of $17.7 billion for the first half of this year.
